question.prompt: Pat Peano has plenty of \(0\)’s, \(1\)’s, \(3\)’s, \(4\)’s, \(5\)’s, \(6\)’s, \(7\)’s, \(8\)’s and \(9\)’s, but he has only twenty-two \(2\)’s. How far can he number the pages of his scrapbook with these digits?

solutions.explanation:
Count every occurrence of the digit \(2\), since a page such as \(22\) uses two copies.

Among pages \(1\) through \(99\), the numbers \(2,12,22,\ldots,92\) use ten \(2\)'s in the ones place. Pages \(20\) through \(29\) use another ten in the tens place. This counts the two separate digits in \(22\) exactly as needed, giving \(20\) copies altogether.

From \(100\) through \(119\), only \(102\) and \(112\) contain a \(2\), using the remaining two copies. Thus Pat can number every page through \(119\). The next page, \(120\), requires a twenty-third \(2\), so he must stop at \(\boxed{119}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Count the 2s by position
